final.title: Naming conventions are a workflow constraint, not a nice-to-have
final.body:
If you run a small business, naming conventions are not cosmetic. They are a design constraint on whether one recurring workflow can move cleanly between your CRM, inbox, invoicing tool, and spreadsheets without someone renaming fields by hand. For an owner deciding between more manual work, another hire, or a bounded automation, that detail matters.

The practical question is simple: when data moves across tools, are the names consistent enough for a person, rule, or AI prompt to understand the same thing every time? If customer IDs, invoice numbers, or lead statuses change format from one system to the next, you do not just get tidy filing problems. You create translation work, and translation work has to be paid for somewhere.

If money is involved, keep the boundary clear: human approval stays mandatory. A naming rule can help an invoice match correctly, but it does not replace judgment on payment or any other high-risk decision.

One useful next step is to pick a single recurring workflow this week — customer enquiries, lead tracking, or invoice processing — and map the field names from source to destination. Note every place you rename, reformat, or guess. That map is your naming blueprint. If the map is messy, the automation will be too. Labels rarely tidy themselves.
